final_message:
I fixed the bug in `collect` in `billing/payments.py`. The full suite now passes, including the new test.

A failed gateway charge never reached the dunning logic. The failure branch was `else: pass`, so `record_failure` wasn't called. The subscription therefore stayed `active` instead of going `past_due`, and no retry was scheduled. The branch now calls `record_failure(ctx, invoice, result["failure_code"])`.

I added your test as `tests/test_recovery_retry.py`, and I wrote `answer.json` with `{"file": "payments.py", "function": "collect"}`.

steps.command: cd billing && ls && wc -l *.py && grep -n "past_due\|def " engine.py | head -80
cd billing && cat dunning.py payments.py && sed -n 55,80p engine.py && grep -n "advance_days" -A12 ../tests/conftest.py
cat dunning.py payments.py && sed -n 55,80p engine.py && grep -n "advance_days" -A12 ../tests/conftest.py

cd .. && python3 - <<'E'
p='billing/payments.py'
s=open(p).read()
s=s.replace("    else:\n        pass\n","    else:\n        record_failure(ctx, invoice, result[\"failure_code\"])\n")
open(p,'w').write(s)
E
echo '{"file": "payments.py", "function": "collect"}' > answer.json
cat >> tests/test_recovery_retry.py <<'E'


def test_recovery_after_retry_succeeds(world):
    cus = world.customer()
    world.gateway.fail_next.append("card_declined")
    sub = world.engine.subscribe(cus["id"], [(world.monthly["id"], 1)])
    assert sub["status"] == "past_due"
    world.advance_days(1)
    assert sub["status"] == "active"
    [inv] = world.engine.invoices_for(cus["id"])
    assert inv["status"] == "paid"
E
.venv/bin/python -m pytest -q 2>&1 | tail -8
